title: 1995 AHSME Problem 23
statement: The sides of a triangle have lengths \(11,\) \(15,\) and \(k,\) where \(k\) is an integer. For how many values of \(k\) is the triangle obtuse?

solutions.text: The triangle inequality gives \(5\le k\le25.\) For \(k\le15,\) the longest side is \(15,\) and the triangle is obtuse when \[ 15^2\gt11^2+k^2, \] which gives \(5\le k\le10,\) or \(6\) values. For \(k\gt15,\) it is obtuse when \(k^2\gt11^2+15^2=346,\) giving \(19\le k\le25,\) or \(7\) values. The total is \(6+7=13,\) so the correct answer is D.
hints: First use the triangle inequality to bound the integer \(k\)
Test the obtuse inequality separately when \(15\) is longest and when \(k\) is longest
